issues.title: getMetaDataSymbol() declares a boxed Symbol
issues.body:
* [x] Are you running the latest version?
* [x] Have you included sample input, output, error, and expected output?
* [x] Have you checked if you are using correct configuration?
* [ ] Did you try online [tool](https://naturalintelligence.github.io/fast-xml-parser/)? Not applicable to TypeScript declarations.
* [x] Have you checked the [docs](https://github.com/NaturalIntelligence/fast-xml-parser/tree/master/docs) for helpful APIs and examples?

### Description

The ESM and CommonJS declarations return boxed `Symbol` from `XMLParser.getMetaDataSymbol()`, preventing direct use as a property key. The implementation returns a primitive `symbol`, with an existing `string` fallback.

### Input

fast-xml-parser 5.11.2, TypeScript 5.9.3. Save as `repro.mts` and run `npx tsc --strict --noEmit --module nodenext repro.mts`.

### Code

```ts
import { XMLParser } from "fast-xml-parser";

const key: PropertyKey = XMLParser.getMetaDataSymbol();
```

### Output

```text
error TS2322: Type 'Symbol' is not assignable to type 'PropertyKey'.
```

### expected data

The assignment should compile. I have a declaration-only fix returning `symbol | string`, with ESM and CommonJS consumer tests.

**Would you like to work on this issue?**

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

comments.body: Just wanted to chime in here: Our project relies on `#text` always being present. We ran into this same bug where `#text` is missing for self-closing elements that have attributes. We're not asking for the same feature the OP is asking for, but would love for that bug to be fixed.
comments.author: kronodeus

comments.body: The scope would be easier to review if the first version defined a small acceptance contract for `alwaysCreateTextNode: true`. I would call out the default behavior, the migration/backwards-compatibility story, and one or two cases that are intentionally out of scope so the implementation does not grow beyond the original request.
comments.author: hiSandog

comments.body:
The missing-text-node behavior reported here for self-closing elements with attributes is fixed by commit 31bbc99adedcada7d52bc4745273e7d8b9824b31, which is included in v5.7.3 and later tags.

I checked current master (80e88a8, package version 5.11.2) with the original workbookPr example plus empty paired tags, boolean attributes, and custom textNodeName, with alwaysCreateTextNode both enabled and disabled: all 16 checks pass. With the option enabled, the attributed self-closing element includes an empty text property; with it disabled, the existing attribute-only output is preserved.

This addresses the missing #text report, but does not add the separate option requested in the opening post to exclude text nodes specifically for self-closing elements.
comments.author: hengweiyv

comments.body: I'll add a short documentation example for the current empty-element behaviour with attributes, covering both values of alwaysCreateTextNode. This will clarify the existing behaviour rather than introduce a new parser option.
